mechanism: Pharmacodynamic synergism: Concurrent administration of an anticoagulant (Warfarin) and an antiplatelet agent (Aspirin) significantly impairs hemostasis.
description: Marked increase in the risk of major gastrointestinal hemorrhage and intracranial bleeding.
recommendation: Avoid concurrent use unless strictly indicated for high-risk cardiac events with vigilant INR monitoring and GI protection (PPI).

mechanism: Pharmacodynamic antiplatelet effect and GI mucosal injury combined with competitive protein binding displacement.
description: NSAIDs damage gastric mucosa and inhibit platelet aggregation, substantially multiplying Warfarin-induced bleeding risk.
recommendation: Avoid NSAID combination. Use Acetaminophen for pain relief or an alternative analgesic under clinical supervision.

mechanism: Pharmacokinetic enzyme inhibition: Clarithromycin is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor that prevents hepatic metabolism of Simvastatin.
description: Substantially increases serum Simvastatin concentrations (up to 10-fold), precipitating severe myopathy and life-threatening rhabdomyolysis.
recommendation: Discontinue Simvastatin therapy temporarily during Clarithromycin course or switch to a non-CYP3A4 metabolized statin (e.g., Pravastatin, Rosuvastatin).

mechanism: Additive pharmacodynamic inhibition of aldosterone secretion and potassium excretion.
description: Significantly elevated risk of severe hyperkalemia, particularly in patients with baseline renal impairment or elderly digital twins.
recommendation: Monitor serum potassium and renal function (creatinine/eGFR) within 1-2 weeks of initiation and regularly thereafter.

mechanism: Hepatic CYP1A2 metabolic inhibition by Ciprofloxacin.
description: Decreased Theophylline clearance leads to toxic serum levels, inducing severe nausea, tachyarrhythmias, and potential seizures.
recommendation: Reduce Theophylline dosage by 30-50% and perform therapeutic drug monitoring if co-administration is strictly required.

mechanism: Inhibition of CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 clearance of S- and R-warfarin enantiomers.
description: Marked prolongation of prothrombin time / INR elevation and severe hemorrhagic complications.
recommendation: Reduce Warfarin dose empirically by 33% to 50% upon initiating Amiodarone; monitor INR weekly.

mechanism: Potential alteration of glycemic control via OCT2/MATE transport modulation.
description: Fluoroquinolones may cause dysglycemia (hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia) in diabetic patients on oral hypoglycemics.
recommendation: Advise patient to increase frequency of self-monitoring of blood glucose levels during antibiotic therapy.

description: Moderate increase in systemic statin exposure, elevating potential for muscle tenderness or transaminase elevation.
recommendation: Limit Atorvastatin dose to maximum 20mg daily during Clarithromycin therapy and monitor for muscle symptoms.
